quickAnalyze.title: Is it real?
quickAnalyze.subtitle: Paste a link or article excerpt. We'll run it through three models in seconds.

trust.label: Personal trust score
trust.copyNone: Run your first check to see your personal trust score.
trust.copyHigh: Most of what you check turns out to be credible. Keep verifying before you share.
trust.copyMixed: Mixed signals — stay alert before sharing what you read.
trust.copyLow: You catch a lot of suspect content. That vigilance protects everyone around you.

recent.heading: Your recent checks
recent.subtitle: The reasoning shown is the model's top flag for each item.
recent.emptyBody: Paste a link in the box above to run your first verification.

emotionalHeadlines.title: Watch for emotional headlines
emotionalHeadlines.body: Sensationalist or fear-inducing headlines are a common signal of low-credibility content. Pause before sharing.

checkSource.title: Check the source
checkSource.body: Unfamiliar domains, lookalike URLs, and missing author bylines are red flags. Search the outlet name independently.

crossReference.title: Cross-reference the story
crossReference.body: Real news is rarely reported by only one outlet. If no other credible source covers it, treat it with suspicion.

readPastHeadline.title: Read past the headline
readPastHeadline.body: Many misleading articles have headlines that don't match the actual content. Read the full piece before forming an opinion.

reverseImage.title: Reverse-image search photos
reverseImage.body: Images are often reused out of context. A quick reverse search can reveal the original date and source.

checkDate.title: Check the date
checkDate.body: Old stories often resurface as if they were new. Always check publication dates before reacting.

perfectQuotes.title: Beware perfect quotes
perfectQuotes.body: Fabricated stories often include suspiciously polished quotes from public figures that can't be verified elsewhere.
